newsitem.title: INDIA: India regrets U.S. expulsion of diplomats.
newsitem.headline: India regrets U.S. expulsion of diplomats.

text.p: India said on Monday it regretted a U.S. decision to expel two Indian diplomats but would still work with Washington to improve friendly relations.
"We deeply regret this decision," a Foreign Ministry spokesman said in a statement released in New Delhi.
A U.S. State Department spokesman said on Sunday Washington had ordered two Indian diplomats to leave the country in retaliation for the expulsion of an American official from New Delhi last month.
Indian officials told Reuters that New Delhi had in fact asked two U.S. diplomats, including the head of the U.S. Central Intelligence Agency (CIA) in New Delhi, to leave the country.
The Indian diplomats, who the Indian spokesman said would be returning to India soon, were carrying out normal duties as consular officers in San Francisco and Chicago, the Foreign Ministry said.
"We categorically reject any implication to the contrary," the ministry spokesman said.

"Viewing this unnecessary incident, in the broader perspective of mature Indo-U.S. relations, India will continue to work with the United States in improving and expanding friendly ties and cooperation," the spokesman said.
Indian officials said the U.S. diplomats had established unauthorised contacts with Rattan Sehgal, heading the anti-espionage division of India's Intelligence Bureau.
Sehgal was asked to resign after the alleged links were discovered. Before expelling the two Indian diplomats, Washington had said the affair was an internal matter within the Indian government.
Some Indian nawspapers have accused the Indian government of bungling Sehgal's sacking, saying it showed a lack of trust in a senior official's integrity.
The Indian government has made no formal comment on the sacking of Sehgal, who had worked in the Foreign Ministry for several years.
